Overview/Data

Dataset · Public records

NYC sales linked to deeds and mortgages

New York City residential sales, 2016–2025, with deed links and nearby recorded mortgage matches for eligible houses and condominiums in the four ACRIS boroughs

By Pablo LoschiData 1.1 · Documentation 1.1.0 · 16 October 2026CC BY 4.0Public dataset
Get dataset and codeRead the data note PDF

Why these records need linking

New York City publishes its property sales and its recorded deeds and mortgages as separate open datasets, and the two do not join directly. The Department of Finance sales file has the price and date but no document number. ACRIS, the city register, has the deeds and mortgages but not the sales. Condominiums are the hardest case: the sales file usually identifies a unit by the building's billing lot, while ACRIS records its deed and mortgage under the unit's own lot, so a join on the parcel number misses most of them.

This dataset links the records using fixed, documented rules. The studies on this site and other researchers can reuse the same matches. The public files contain no party names.

In numbers

  • 729,047house, condominium and co-operative sales, 2016–2025, all five boroughs
  • 97.2%eligible house sales with a deed link in release 1.1.0

Condominium deed-link counts and mortgage statistics are being recomputed. The earlier combined figures and mortgage comparison chart are withheld here until those checks are complete. The dated 1.1.0 download remains available.

Files in the deposited 1.1.0 dataset

Three tables that share keys: sales joins to links on sale_id, and links joins to deed_flags on deed_document_id. A blank cell means not applicable or not measured, never zero.

Files and main columns
FileRowsMain columns
sales.csv.gz729,047Borough, block and lot; property group (house, condo, co-op); building class; address; price; sale date; geography; flags for ACRIS coverage and the $300,000–$6 million band
links.csv.gz729,047Deed match (unique, none, ambiguous); ACRIS deed id; recovered unit lot; financed in three windows (30, 90 and 180 days); number of mortgages; largest loan amount and its document id; CEMA flag
deed_flags.csv.gz296,165Party counts; company, trust or estate buyer; same surname (and a strict version); shared mailing address; lender name; deed event from the foreclosure paper's classifier; legal-rule amount

The download also includes the raw extracts and their retrieval records, Python code using the standard library, and CODEBOOK.md, which defines every column and rule.

How the link works

  • Deed. A deed matches a sale when its amount is within 0.5% of the price and its date within 45 days. Houses are matched on their own parcel. Condominiums are matched within the block among unit lots, which recovers the unit; it agrees with the sales file's own unit lot in 99.3% of single-parcel links. If deeds on two parcels qualify, the sale is left unlinked rather than guessed. If several deeds qualify on the same parcel, the lowest document identifier is kept, which picks one without showing which is correct; this happens for 916 of the 297,252 links.
  • Mortgage. A sale receives a recorded-mortgage flag if a mortgage is recorded on its parcel (for condominiums, the recovered unit) from 15 days before to 30, 90 or 180 days after the sale. A recorded mortgage is not verified purchase finance.
  • Flags. Computed from the ACRIS party records of each deed, with the papers' own rules. Party names were used to compute flags and are excluded from the public release. The flags are a fixed snapshot.

Archived agreement checks for release 1.1.0

The financing flags agree with the archived panel of The Shape of the Tax for every one of 166,736 houses and all but 4 of 82,348 condominiums. Recomputing that paper's mortgage-recording-tax table from this dataset reproduces every reported statistic. Since that paper's version 2.5 takes its condominium loans from this dataset, that row is no longer an independent comparison. These checks show that the computations agree with earlier code, not that the links are accurate. Against the repeat-sale pairs of Who Gets the House?, the linked deed is the same at 15,902 endpoints and different at 1.

Limits

  • A financed flag of 0 means no mortgage was recorded on the parcel in the window. It is not proof of a cash purchase.
  • Co-operative and Staten Island sales are listed but never linked. ACRIS real-property mortgages do not measure financing secured by co-op shares, and Staten Island deeds are outside ACRIS.
  • Condominium linkage counts in the deposited 1.1.0 release reflect the incorrect unit-lot ceiling. Corrected counts and the resulting mortgage statistics are under review.
  • The company, surname, address and deed-event flags are screens built from names. Existing review agreement does not establish independently verified population accuracy. The party records are not deposited, so these flags are supplied as a fixed snapshot.

Condominium coverage

The former borough comparison reflected an incorrect unit-lot limit in my code. It should not be interpreted as evidence of missing public records. Read the correction.

Coverage measures how many records link. Accuracy requires checking the links against source documents.

Try the data

Start with the two-example guide. It explains how to extract the data and examples into one folder, then produce annual condominium coverage and a comparison of linked and unlinked sales using standard Python. The commands reproduce data release 1.0. To get the 1.1.0 coverage table from the first example, replace build/links.csv.gz with the 1.1.0 file of the same name before running it; the second example checks the 1.0 counts and runs only with the 1.0 links file. If you try it, tell me what worked or where you got stuck.

python3 examples/recorded_mortgage_example.py build --output annual_condo_coverage.csv
python3 examples/condo_selection.py build --output selection
